prompt: 10 million order records — two different operations:

options.label: Row store: "fetch order #4821821, all fields"
options.content: Every field of that one order is stored physically together on disk - one read returns the customer ID, product, quantity, price, shipping address, and timestamp all at once, in one contiguous chunk. This is fast and natural for a row store; it's exactly the access pattern it's built around.

options.label: Column store: "average order_value across all 10 million orders"
options.content: Only the order_value column's data needs to be read - every other field (customer ID, shipping address, timestamps) lives in separate physical blocks that this query never has to touch at all. A row store answering the same question would have to read every full record just to pull out one field from each - the column store skips everything it doesn't need.
